newsitem.title: UK: British bankers warned of bond theft in 1995 - assn.
newsitem.headline: British bankers warned of bond theft in 1995 - assn.

text.p: The British Bankers Association (BBA) said on Monday it had warned its members of the theft and subsequent resurfacing of stolen bonds from Citibank as early as 1995.
Citibank confirmed on Monday some cancelled certificates, which were thought to have been destroyed in the mid-1980s, had resurfaced.

The bank made a statement following a report in the Evening Standard newspaper that it had retained a British private detective, Chris Morris, to recover bonds with an estimated face value of at least $111 billion stolen from a waste disposal company.
But Citibank said it had no material financial exposure to any of the securities. It also said it had never had a contract with a private detective to recover them.
A BBA spokesman said its members were alerted to the incident through its fraud intelligence unit early in 1995.
"We're reassured that members had adequate warning of this," he said. "We were on the trail of it through the fraud unit well before the bonds actually surfaced."

He said that as with any sort of false paper, a warning notice was sent as soon the BBA became aware of any risk. The spokesman said he did not have an estimate of the amount of bonds, in terms of face value, which had resurfaced. He also said the BBA was not aware of any recent occurrences of stolen bonds resurfacing, although that did not mean none had.
Citibank in its statement said cancelled securities which had resurfaced had been fraudulently presented.

"In 1985-86 Citibank used an outside destruction firm, MSM Corp, to dispose of a number of cancelled certificates. Subsequently the bank discovered that a number of these certificates thought to have been destroyed had reappeared and some have been fraudulently presented for transfer or offered as collateral for loans," the bank statement said.

"Citibank is not able to provide details of any specific joint recovery activities with the City of London Police or any other law enforcement authority. However, we strongly refute any allegation that Chris Morris had a contract with Citibank," the bank added.
The Evening Standard reported that Morris was used as part of a complex sting operation set up in 1995 by the City of London and the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) to recover the stolen bonds.
